Guidance & outlook: On the oil p alm plantation front, the company generated highest-ever quarterly revenue of INR740 crores in Q1 FY27.
Turning now to our FMCG segment, the quarterly revenue stood at INR2,9 38 crores with EBITDA of INR190 crores and EBITDA margin of 6.45% in Q1 FY27.
Revenue from consumer staples segment stood at more than INR1,000 crores in Q1 FY27.
Growth & demand: Our beverage portfolio generated revenue of INR38 crores, driven by extended summers aided by delayed onset of monsoon, as well as new product launches including mango chutney, mango panna juice, and orange juice.

I want to reaffirm our full -year guidance range we h ave laid out for the business, edible oil margin construct between 3% to 5% volume growth for the year , food and FMCG 8% to 10% growth with beauty and personal care growing at around 15%, FMCG vertical EBITDA growth at 12% to 15% for the year.

So growth sequentially if I look at the previous quarter itself, the revenues on staples have grown almost INR260 crores which is 30% growth, and we grew our ethnic food side where there was some contraction that we witnessed.
Margins & costs: Operating EBITDA for the period was INR543 crores with a margin at 4.80%, while profit before tax stood at INR453 crores, translating into PBT margin of 4%.

Within FMCG by category, the biscuits generated revenue of INR560 crores, registering Patanjali Foods Limited August 17, 2026 year-on-year growth of 27%, reflecting continued consumer trust and preference, with EBITDA margin of 15.35% versus 9.35% in the same period last year.

This is working in our favor, offsetting much of the input cost pressure elsewhere in the portfolio and keeps us on course to deliver both the growth and the overall margin construct we have Patanjali Foods Limited August 17, 2026 guided to for the company, even after accounting for the raw material inflation flowing through from delayed monsoon.
Capex & expansion: So this quarter, for example, we did nearly 15% plus in EBITDA on the on the biscuit , and I would say that very substantial part of that has been driven by at the back of the success of Doodh Biscuit on continued expansion.
So, I have a question that we have acquired, we have paid INR1,100 crores and we have acquired Patanjali Ayurved's Home and Personal Care business.
The first one that we acquired was biscuits business, then we acquired the foods business, and then we acquired the HPC business.
Risks & challenges: Ghee sales were softer during the quarter and generated revenue of INR219 crores, reflecting the seasonal nature of demand and lower summer off -take in export -oriented markets, particularly in the Middle East, where geopolitical tensions disrupted normal c onsumption and trade patterns.

Despite some delay in the monsoon, recent data on sowing of Kharif, including rice, pulses, coarse cereals, sugarcane, et c, has showcased resilience.Acreage gap has narrowed to 1.9% vis-à-vis last year.

The soya oil price futures increased by 40% towards the end of March and then stabilized towards the end of June, the FOB prices corrected by 6% amidst lower demand, leading to a sharper decline in physical prices with further firming similar to palm oil price trend.

So that we are positive ourselves and we have in any case given a guidance of 8% to 10% growth on the staples side in the overall food business also, and we pretty much stay true to that.
